cues.en:
"Let's do a feature on our school's
seven wonders in the next paper!"

With that one remark from our club president,
our newspaper club ended up featuring them.

This summer, the old school building,
unused for years, was to be torn down,

and he wanted a horror piece
to go with it.

And I, still a first-year and the newest member,
ended up being put in charge of it.

But I didn't really know what scary stories
had been handed down at this school.

So my upperclassman offered to bring people
who knew the seven wonders to the club room.

But he had something to do and couldn't come,
so I'd have to run things myself.

I wouldn't know who the seven were
until I met them.

Apparently the seven would gather
in the club room after school today.

I'm not good with scary stories.
If anything, I'm a bit of a coward.

Today, dull gray clouds
filled the whole sky.
It looked like it could rain any minute.

Even the wind was damp,
clinging to my skin.

Why did I have to hear scary stories
in a dim club room on a day like this?
I was starting to want to run away.

And yet, against my will,
my feet were carrying me to the club room.

Maybe, deep down, part of me
wanted to see something scary.
